records.rationale: All three ledger cases are delivered on main and each was reproduced by an independent verifier. S1 (route without spec fails; spec without route fails): vizra-core #18 made the contract test walk wildcard routes and fail closed on shapes it cannot map; the verifier's own mutations on the real router went red in both directions. S2 (generated client diff empty after regeneration) and N1 (hand-edited generated file rejected): vizra-user #12 re-vendored the contract at core 5f615d7 and added an exact six-operation test; the verifier re-vendored from core main with no diff and saw the drift check reject a hand edit. IMPLEMENTED, not VERIFIED: the ledger's evidence_required asks for CI job output of the both-direction drift failure on a deliberate mutation, and every red run so far is a verifier-local transcript. Known limits, recorded in docs/warroom/FOLLOWUPS.md: no CI compares vizra-user's vendored contract with core main; the worker's metrics mux is outside what the contract test walks.

acceptance.bullet: (VZ-FOUND-002) Route-without-spec and spec-without-route both fail CI (demonstrated)
(VZ-FOUND-002) Generated client diff is empty after regeneration
(VZ-FOUND-002) Hand-edited generated file is rejected by a drift check

records.rationale: IMPLEMENTED, not VERIFIED: one outcome clause is not delivered. There is no compatibility window: migrate-lint rejects destructive statements in every up file unless the line before carries `-- allow-destructive: <reason>`, and nothing checks the reason, requires a review, or ties the marker to a release boundary, so a marked column drop that breaks the previous release passes (independent verifier, meta #25 round 1, reproduced on vizra-core a6d4792). What owning the window means is owner inbox 21. The five ledger cases are on vizra-core main, each reproduced by an independent verifier. S1 (`migrate up` from the release image on an empty DB): vizra-core #19 runs `vizra migrate` from the built runtime image against an empty, digest-pinned PostgreSQL twice in docker-build and checks the ledger reads the head version, not dirty, both times; CI red on a broken migration (job 131221389383), green on the merged head (job 131223440387). R1 (dirty ledger reported, not auto-fixed): #19's integration test makes a real ledger dirty and asserts refusal naming the version with nothing repaired; red on a mutation (job 131217791460), green ordered and shuffled with no skips (build-test run 43230273284). N1 (an unmarked DROP COLUMN fails migrate-lint): vizra-core #18, with a differential test that the script never accepts what the earlier one rejected. S2 (sqlc-verify) and N2 (editing sqlcgen output fails the drift check): `make ci` and an sqlcgen edit on main, both run by build-test (`==> migrate-lint`, `==> sqlc-verify`).
